A.biggest_strength: Exceptional conceptual clarity through the unifying mathematical formula (ack = seq + len + SYN + FIN), disciplined color-coding of byte streams and phantom bytes, and live tracking of internal TCP state counters (SND.NXT and RCV.NXT).
A.biggest_weakness: Lacks free-form numeric text inputs for students to type arbitrary sequence numbers and payload lengths, providing three presets instead.

B.biggest_strength: Interactive flexibility that allows users to type arbitrary 32-bit ISNs and payload byte lengths, alongside a random 32-bit ISN generator and Wireshark-style relative numbers toggle.
B.biggest_weakness: Broken mobile layout at 390 px phone width caused by a 480 px min-width SVG in an overflow container, completely truncating the server lifeline, server states, and arrowheads off-screen.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is the clear winner because it transforms complex protocol mechanics into intuitive visual knowledge. Its core equation (ack = seq + len + SYN + FIN) immediately resolves the classic student confusion around SYN and FIN sequence consumption, reinforced by color-coded stream tracking, live SND.NXT/RCV.NXT state variables, and real Linux tcpdump verification. While Page B provides great numeric input flexibility, its mobile view severely fails by clipping the entire server half of the diagram off-screen, whereas Page A reflows seamlessly across screen sizes.
